$meta.name: Error envelope
$meta.description: The shape of every error body an API returns (ERROR-6), and the codes too generic to replace a more specific sentence. Clients read the facts their copy needs from these fields; they never parse the English `message` for meaning.

provenance.babel: babel-lambda-api error.middleware.ts sends status, errorCode, message, details and fieldErrors; `reference` sits only in details.reference, and only on driver faults. A top-level reference on every 5xx is wave A of the clear-errors program.
provenance.rendee: groome-nodeJS apps/api sends requestId on every error body and an errorCode on very few. `reference` is added beside requestId.

$meta.compatibilityNote: Every field below except status, errorCode and message is optional and additive. Released clients ignore a field they do not know, so adding one is safe; changing a status code that released mobile clients parse is not, and goes behind a client opt-in.

status.doc: Always false on an error. A body without a boolean status is not our envelope (a gateway or CDN page): the client classifies it as front_door, timeout, rate_limited, too_large or outdated_client from the HTTP status (ERRORS.md section 3).

errorCode.doc: A code as specific as the message (COPY-2). Clients switch on it and render their own localized copy. See error-codes.json.

message.doc: The server's sentence, localized for the caller where the server can. A client shows it only when it is localized and the code is not in genericCodes.

details.doc: The facts the copy needs: the gate, the field, the entity, the provider. Shapes below.

details.gate.doc: On a 403 (and a 402): which gate refused, so the client names it (ERROR-5) and never guesses (TRUTH-1). See `gate`.

fieldErrors.doc: On a 400/422: one entry per field, with an error.field.* code and its params. See field-error-codes.json.

retryAfterSeconds.doc: On a 429 or 503: when a retry is allowed. The same value as the Retry-After header, for clients that cannot read headers.

reference.doc: On every 5xx (ERROR-7): the first `reference.serverLength` characters of the logged request id, written to the same log line. Shown to the person with a way to copy it.

fields.required: The permissions that would pass, as `<section>.<action>` strings.
fields.roles: The roles that hold them, as role keys the client translates.
fields.grantor: Who can grant it, as a role key (for example `president`), never a person's name.

headers.doc: Every API lists these in its CORS exposed headers, so a browser client can read them.

reference.doc: A server reference is 8 characters of the logged request id. A client that has no server reference (a crash, a server that did not answer) mints `E-` plus 6 uppercase hex characters and sends it to its crash reporter under the same id.

genericCodesNote: Names in error-codes.json. A code listed here never replaces a more specific sentence: the server does not attach it to a throw whose message is more specific, and localization never swaps such a message for the code's catalogue line (ERROR-6).
